message.content:
Nicolaus Copernicus faced criticism from several scholars and religious authorities during and after his lifetime. The Catholic Church later placed *De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium* on the Index of Banned Books in 1616. Martin Luther reportedly dismissed the heliocentric model, calling its proponent a "foolish schoolmaster" who tried to turn the world upside down. Tycho Brahe rejected the idea of Earth's motion in favor of his own geocentric-heliocentric hybrid model.

Who were the most significant critics of Copernicus's heliocentric theory? How did the Church respond to the challenges posed by Copernican astronomy? Why did some contemporary astronomers accept the mathematics but reject the physical implications? What were the theological objections that scholars like Andreas Osiander raised in his controversial preface to the first edition?

How revolutionary was it to propose that the Earth moved around the Sun! What a bold challenge to the established Ptolemaic worldview! How remarkable was the courage it took to publish such a radical idea! How much influence these critics had on the delayed acceptance of heliocentrism!
